source.quote: NuPrime's own page for the DAC-8, read 2026-11-25 in full, input list: « USB : Type B 2.0 Hi-Speed, Windows OS : data stream up to 384KHz/24Bit and Native DSD 256. »; « USB : Type B 2.0 Hi-Speed, Mac / Lunix OS : data stream up to 384KHz/24Bit and DOP DSD 128. » - the misspelling « Lunix » is the page's; « IIS/DSD : Supports PCM 44.1KHz ~ 384KHz/32Bit and DSD 64 ~ DSD 256 data streams. »; « OPTICAL : Supports PCM 44.1KHz ~ 192KHz/24Bit and DOP 64. »; « COAXIAL : Supports PCM 44.1KHz ~ 384KHz/24Bit and DOP 64 and 128. »; « EXTENSION : Supports PCM 44.1KHz ~ 192KHz/24Bit. » The specification text names NO converter. A third-party review quoted on the page says « Featuring the ESS ES9018Q2C chip and NuPrime's custom SRC IC for DSP processing ». A volume FAQ says « The DAC's analog output ... go through a low noise and low distortion resistance ladder circuit design (implemented as an IC) ». No digital filter, oversampling or NOS row.

facts.chip: NOT NAMED by the maker. The only part number on the page, « the ESS ES9018Q2C chip », is inside a quoted third-party review, and a review is not the maker's specification.

_verification_des_conditions_faite: nuprimeaudio.com has no terms-of-use page: the footer offers Contact & Support, a Privacy Policy, Facebook and an email address. The privacy policy WAS READ and carries no clause on copying, reproducing or extracting site content. The footer reads « Copyright 2026 (c) Nuprime Audio, Inc. --- brand managed by Nuoem Pte. Ltd. », the ordinary notice.
_la_puce_est_dans_une_CITATION_DE_PRESSE: « Featuring the ESS ES9018Q2C chip and NuPrime's custom SRC IC » - inside a review the maker reproduces on its own page. The maker hosting a review does not make the review's claims its own, and the sibling DAC-9X names its converter in its own words two models up the range. family stays `unknown`. Second time in two days a review on a maker's page has offered a fact the record refuses, after the Audiolab D7's « filter selection ».
_une_echelle_de_resistances_qui_nest_PAS: « a low noise and low distortion resistance ladder circuit design (implemented as an IC) ». The words « resistance ladder » on a DAC page are exactly what a search for R-2R would catch - and the sentence is about the VOLUME control. The DAC-10H's page carries the same trap in almost the same words. Noted so nobody files this device as a ladder converter.
